bib.title: Annotation Artifacts in Natural Language Inference Data

question: Do the crowdsourcing protocols behind SNLI and MultiNLI leave hypothesis-only clues that let a classifier predict the label without the premise, and how much of NLI model accuracy depends on them?
hypothesis: Crowd workers adopt heuristics when writing hypotheses, producing annotation artifacts that models exploit, so reported NLI performance is overestimated.
contributions: Show a premise-oblivious classifier beats the majority baseline on SNLI and MultiNLI
Characterise artifacts by lexical choice (PMI) and sentence length
Split test sets into Hard and Easy and re-evaluate DAM, ESIM, DIIN
Release the Hard SNLI and MultiNLI test sets

method.summary: Train fastText on the hypothesis only to predict the NLI label; analyse word-class PMI and length; split each test set into Easy (hypothesis-only model correct) and Hard (incorrect) and evaluate three retrained NLI models on full, Hard and Easy.
method.task: natural language inference (3-way: entailment, neutral, contradiction)

datasets.name: SNLI
datasets.source: Bowman et al. 2015, premises from image captions

datasets.name: MultiNLI
datasets.split: original train; matched and mismatched test
datasets.preprocessing: MultiNLI models trained on MultiNLI alone, not blended with SNLI

models.name: fastText (hypothesis only)
models.architecture: bag of words and bigrams text classifier

other.MultiNLI extras: character 4-grams; words seen fewer than 10 times in training filtered

models.name: ESIM
models.architecture: Enhanced Sequential Inference Model (Chen et al. 2017)

models.name: DIIN
models.architecture: Densely Interactive Inference Network (Gong et al. 2018)

training.objective: supervised classification of the NLI label

other.NLI models: All models were retrained out of the box (public implementations); no hyperparameters given

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: share of test examples classified correctly (inferred from Table 2/5 values in %)

metrics.name: PMI(word, class)
metrics.definition: log p(word,class)/(p(word,.)p(.,class)) over training set, add-100 smoothing

baselines: logistic regression with word and character n-gram features
eval.protocol: Easy = test examples the premise-oblivious model got right, Hard = the rest; single run, no seeds or significance test stated.

availability.code: third-party implementations: allennlp (DAM), nyu-mll/multiNLI (ESIM), DIIN link
availability.data: Hard SNLI and MultiNLI matched/mismatched test sets released via short links (goo.gl)

results.claim: Median length of a neutral SNLI hypothesis is 9 tokens, and 60% of entailments have 7 tokens or less.

results.claim: 8.8% of entailed SNLI hypotheses are fully contained (bag of words) in their premise, against 0.2% of neutrals and contradictions.
results.quote: 8.8% of entailed hypotheses in SNLI are fully contained within their premise, while only 0.2% of neutrals and contradictions exhibit the same property.

results.claim: Negation words are strong contradiction cues: 'no' appears in 7.6% of MultiNLI contradiction training sentences and 'never' in 5.0%.
results.setup: Top PMI words, MultiNLI contradiction class
results.table: Table 4, row MNLI, Contradiction column, word no
results.note: never 5.0%; SNLI sleeping 3.2%, outside 8.0% for entailment

results.claim: Removing Easy examples may not give an artifact-free set: dropping contradictions with 'no' moves the word to neutral and entailment classes, creating a new artifact.

limits: Only fastText was used to define Hard/Easy; other classifiers said to give similar results but not shown.
NLI models retrained out of the box with no hyperparameters, seeds or variance reported.
Hard set is defined by one model's failures so Hard examples may carry new artifacts; filtering training data left to future work.
Dataset sizes are not stated in the paper.
Artifacts are diverse and individually infrequent; analysis is shallow and statistical.
Authors note artifacts do not make examples wrong; the problem is a skewed sample distribution.

terms.definition: patterns in the data produced by the framing of the annotation task and the language generation choices crowd workers make
examples the premise-oblivious model classified accurately are Easy, and those it could not are Hard
